svg.text: Actual Jones rows: two failed balancing shortcuts
Index four; full all-smooth amenability is proved. Algebra boxes are schematic.
The physical inclusion and its ordinary tunnel
M = Q ⊗ D N = 1(q₀) ⊗ Q≥₁ ⊗ D
Lⱼ = 1(q₀,…,qⱼ₋₁) ⊗ Q≥ⱼ ⊗ D
Bell cup fⱼ = ½ Σ Eab(qⱼ) Eab(qⱼ₊₁); E(fⱼ) = ¼ · 1
Actual core: S = 1(q₀) ⊗ Q≥₁, R = Q. Z(S) = Z(R) = ℂ; every row has J = 0.
A right move destroys one fixed physical target
Before: k = 2ᵐ; k² Weyl columns
hₘ = k⁻² qₘ; Tr(qₘ) = k²
Fresh dₘ₊₁ coordinate is the trace-vector line.
Fixed s = diag(1,−1) in q₁ commutes with hₘ.
‖s hₘ s* − hₘ‖₁ = 0
Right move
q₁ ↔ dₘ₊₁
After: h′ₘ = vₘ hₘ v*ₘ
q′ₘ = vₘ qₘ v*ₘ; q′ₘ s q′ₘ = 0
q′ₘ and s q′ₘ s* are orthogonal.
Both supports still have canonical trace k².
‖s h′ₘ s* − h′ₘ‖₁ = 2
Both row sums, exact physical marginal, compatibility and J = 0 survive the move.
Rows aₘ and s aₘ have the same initial density, but outputs at distance 2.
Thus this operation is not determined by h alone. Proofs: V10.7–V10.10.
Right-sum-one rows do not approximate every compatible balanced state
Fixed physical tail p = E₁₁(d₁); fixed test T = right multiplication by p ∈ A.
Columns E₁₁, E₂₁: left sum 1, right sum 2p. Add an increasing Weyl tail.
Actual central compatible cluster: φ(T) = 1.
Every right-sum-one row: ψ(T) = ½.
The actual centers are scalar, so this φ already satisfies the original joint identity.
A different suitable balanced state exists. Existence is not refuted. Proofs: V10.11–V10.14.
The full compact alternative still requires the unrestricted amenability step
Kbal = ⋂ε>0 weak* closure {coisometric Jones-row states with J ≤ ε}
Exactly the compatible original-trace states satisfying φ ι = φ ι P₀, including singular states.
Either a central state in Kbal gives simultaneous small J and physical defects;
or a fixed finite commutator sum H has ψₐ(H) ≥ c₀ > 0 whenever Jₐ ≤ ε₀.
Full all-smooth amenability must exclude that separator. No exclusion is assumed here.
Proofs: V10.15–V10.18. Full marked corners, residual partition and generating scope remain.
Human context: S. Popa (1994), Definition 3.1.1. Original diagram: CC0-1.0.
